groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: First morning at an internship

dialogue.speaker: Ms Pranee
dialogue.text: Morning, Tawan. Welcome to Lumen Fold Studio. Did you manage to find us all right?

dialogue.speaker: Tawan
dialogue.text: Yes, thanks, although I got off at the wrong bus stop and had to walk the last bit. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Pranee
dialogue.text: Not at all. We said nine, and it's only five to. Before anything else, though, could you sign this confidentiality form? Some of our clients' packaging hasn't been released yet.

dialogue.speaker: Tawan
dialogue.text: Of course. ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Pranee
dialogue.text: Not until the products are actually on the shelves, no. After that, you're welcome to include anything you've contributed to.

dialogue.speaker: Tawan
dialogue.text: That's fair. So what will I be doing this week?

dialogue.speaker: Ms Pranee
dialogue.text: Mostly shadowing me. ___3___ You'll learn more from sitting in on one client meeting than from any textbook.

dialogue.speaker: Tawan
dialogue.text: No, that sounds really useful. Is there anything I should prepare for tomorrow's meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Ms Pranee
dialogue.text: ___4___ Just bring a notebook and save your questions for afterwards. This client can be a little sensitive about outsiders.

options: Did you get the email I sent last night?
I hope I haven't kept you waiting.
Would it be all right if I left early today?
Could you tell me which stop I should use?
items.explanationTh: Ms Pranee ตอบว่า "Not at all. We said nine, and it's only five to." คือยืนยันว่า Tawan ไม่ได้มาสายและไม่ได้ทำให้ใครรอ ตัวลวงเรื่องป้ายรถเมล์หรืออีเมลไม่เข้ากับคำตอบเรื่องเวลา และการขอกลับก่อนไม่สอดคล้องกับ "Not at all" ที่ตามด้วยการบอกเวลานัด

options: Does that mean I can't show this work in my portfolio?
Is it all right if I post photos of the studio online?
Should I hand it in to the HR office by Friday?
Will I be designing packaging for these clients myself?
items.explanationTh: คำตอบ "Not until the products are actually on the shelves, no. After that, you're welcome to include anything you've contributed to." บอกว่าใส่ผลงานได้หลังสินค้าวางขาย จึงต้องเป็นคำถามเรื่องการนำงานไปใส่พอร์ตโฟลิโอ ตัวลวงเรื่องโพสต์รูปสตูดิโอดูใกล้เคียงแต่คำว่า include anything you've contributed to หมายถึงผลงาน ไม่ใช่รูปสถานที่

options: I'm afraid I won't be in the studio at all this week.
I know that doesn't sound very exciting, but bear with me.
Most interns skip this part, so feel free to do the same.
You'll be running your own client project from day one.
items.explanationTh: Tawan ตอบว่า "No, that sounds really useful." ซึ่งเป็นการปฏิเสธความคิดที่ว่างานนี้น่าเบื่อ ผู้พูดจึงต้องออกตัวว่าการติดตามดูงานอาจฟังไม่น่าตื่นเต้น ตัวลวงอื่นขัดกับ "Mostly shadowing me" ทั้งการคุมโปรเจกต์เอง การไม่อยู่สตูดิโอ และการข้ามขั้นตอนนี้

options: Make sure you ask the client plenty of questions.
Nothing beyond what you'd normally bring.
Yes, I'd like you to present our first draft.
You'd better prepare a short talk about yourself.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคต่อมา "Just bring a notebook and save your questions for afterwards" แสดงว่าไม่ต้องเตรียมอะไรพิเศษ ตัวลวงให้นำเสนองาน เตรียมแนะนำตัว หรือถามลูกค้าเยอะ ๆ ขัดกับคำว่า Just และการเก็บคำถามไว้ถามทีหลัง

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: A problem the night before a deadline

dialogue.speaker: Fern
dialogue.text: Sorry to message so late, but I've just spotted something in our survey data. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Oat
dialogue.text: Seriously? That would explain why our totals looked suspiciously high. How many are affected?

dialogue.speaker: Fern
dialogue.text: Around forty. If we take them out, our main finding doesn't really hold up any more.

dialogue.speaker: Kaew
dialogue.text: ___2___ The report's due at nine tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: Oat
dialogue.text: True. So why don't we ask Mr Lerd for a couple of extra days and explain exactly what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Fern
dialogue.text: ___3___ He did tell us that mistakes are fine as long as we're open about them.

dialogue.speaker: Kaew
dialogue.text: All right. ___4___

dialogue.speaker: Fern
dialogue.text: Thanks, Kaew. I'll start cleaning up the data in the meantime.

options: Lots of the Year 11 responses seem to have been entered twice.
A few of the Year 11 responses seem to be missing completely.
The Year 11 forms were collected after the survey closed.
The spreadsheet won't open on my laptop for some reason.
items.explanationTh: Oat บอกว่าข้อมูลนี้อธิบายได้ว่าทำไมยอดรวมสูงผิดปกติ จึงต้องเป็นคำตอบที่ถูกกรอกซ้ำ ตัวลวง "missing" ทำให้ยอดรวมต่ำ ไม่ใช่สูง ส่วนไฟล์เปิดไม่ได้หรือเก็บแบบสอบถามหลังปิดรับไม่ได้ทำให้ยอดรวมสูงขึ้น

options: We can't possibly redo the whole analysis tonight.
Luckily, we've got the whole weekend to fix it.
Then let's just leave the figures as they are.
I'm sure Mr Lerd won't notice the difference.
items.explanationTh: Kaew พูดต่อว่ารายงานต้องส่งเก้าโมงเช้า และ Oat ตอบ "True." แล้วเสนอขอเลื่อนส่ง แสดงว่า Kaew ชี้ปัญหาว่าทำใหม่ไม่ทันคืนนี้ ตัวลวง "leave the figures" และ "won't notice" ไม่ใช่สิ่งที่ Oat จะตอบรับว่า True แล้วเสนอให้บอกครู และ "the whole weekend" ขัดกับกำหนดส่งพรุ่งนี้

options: He'll never agree to that, so let's not bother.
I think he'd be more understanding than you might expect.
We asked him for more time last week as well.
I'd rather we kept the mistake to ourselves.
items.explanationTh: Fern ให้เหตุผลสนับสนุนว่า "He did tell us that mistakes are fine as long as we're open about them." จึงต้องเป็นความเห็นว่าครูน่าจะเข้าใจ ตัวลวงที่บอกว่าครูไม่ยอมหรือให้ปิดเรื่องไว้ขัดกับเหตุผลนี้ และการเคยขอเลื่อนมาแล้วไม่ได้รับการสนับสนุนจากประโยคต่อมา

options: You'd better start cleaning the data, then.
I'll write to him now and copy you both in.
Could you write to him, Fern? I'm exhausted.
Let's tell him after we've handed it in.
items.explanationTh: Fern ตอบว่า "Thanks, Kaew. I'll start cleaning up the data in the meantime." แสดงว่า Kaew อาสาทำบางอย่างให้ (เขียนอีเมลถึงครู) ระหว่างนั้น Fern จึงไปทำความสะอาดข้อมูล ตัวลวงที่ขอให้ Fern เขียนเองทำให้คำขอบคุณไม่สมเหตุผล และการสั่งให้ Fern ทำความสะอาดข้อมูลไม่เข้ากับ "in the meantime" และ "Thanks"

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: End-of-internship feedback

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rattana
dialogue.text: So, Pete, your six weeks with us are almost over. Before I write your report, ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Pete
dialogue.text: Overall, really well. The customer data project taught me a lot, though I struggled to manage my time in the first couple of weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rattana
dialogue.text: ___2___ You took on far more than we asked of you, and some of it slipped.

dialogue.speaker: Pete
dialogue.text: That's true. I found it hard to say no whenever someone asked for help.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rattana
dialogue.text: It's a very common problem. Next time, ___3___ That way, people can see you're not simply refusing.

dialogue.speaker: Pete
dialogue.text: That's really helpful advice. ___4___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rattana
dialogue.text: I'd be happy to. Just send me a reminder nearer the time, as I'll probably need one!

options: could you tell me where you're applying to study?
have you finished the customer data project yet?
I'd like to hear how you think it went.
would you mind signing the attendance sheet?
items.explanationTh: Pete ตอบว่า "Overall, really well." แล้วประเมินตัวเองทั้งข้อดีและข้อที่ต้องปรับ จึงต้องเป็นคำขอให้เล่าว่าการฝึกงานเป็นอย่างไร ตัวลวงถามว่าทำโปรเจกต์เสร็จหรือยังเป็นคำถาม yes/no ที่ "really well" ไม่ได้ตอบ ส่วนเรื่องที่เรียนต่อและการเซ็นชื่อไม่สอดคล้องกับคำตอบ

options: Time management isn't something interns need.
I hadn't noticed any problems with that at all.
That's why we've decided not to write a report.
I'd put that down to enthusiasm rather than carelessness.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคถัดมา "You took on far more than we asked of you" อธิบายว่าปัญหาเกิดจากความกระตือรือร้นรับงานมากเกินไป จึงต้องเป็น "put that down to enthusiasm" (มองว่าเกิดจากความกระตือรือร้น) ตัวลวง "hadn't noticed any problems" ขัดกับ "some of it slipped" และอีกสองตัวเลือกขัดกับบริบทที่กำลังจะเขียนรายงานและให้คำแนะนำ

options: just agree to everything and stay a bit later.
ask your manager to say no on your behalf.
turn people down straight away without a reason.
try explaining what you're already working on before you decline.
items.explanationTh: "That way, people can see you're not simply refusing" แสดงว่าคำแนะนำคือให้อธิบายเหตุผล (งานที่ทำอยู่) ก่อนปฏิเสธ ตัวลวง "without a reason" ตรงข้ามกับใจความ การรับทุกงานขัดกับปัญหาที่เพิ่งพูด และการให้หัวหน้าปฏิเสธแทนไม่ได้ทำให้ผู้อื่นเห็นว่าเขาไม่ได้แค่ปฏิเสธเฉย ๆ

options: Would you act as a referee when I apply to university?
Will the report be sent to my school automatically?
Would you mind if I left a little early on Friday?
Could I possibly have a copy of the report today?
items.explanationTh: Ms Rattana ตอบว่า "I'd be happy to. Just send me a reminder nearer the time" แสดงว่าเป็นคำขอให้ช่วยในอนาคต จึงเป็นการขอให้เป็นผู้รับรอง (referee) ตอนสมัครมหาวิทยาลัย ตัวลวง "today" ขัดกับ "nearer the time" ส่วน "Would you mind" ตอบด้วย "I'd be happy to" ไม่ได้ และคำถามว่าส่งอัตโนมัติไหมไม่ใช่คำขอที่ต้องตอบว่ายินดี

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Checking sources for a group project

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: Come in, both of you. Your teacher mentioned you needed some help with the sources for your project on Khlong Saen Rak?

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: Yes, please. ___1___ but we're not sure which of it we can actually trust.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: Well, that's a good problem to have. Let's see what you've got.

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: This blog says the canal was dug in 1840, but the district office website says 1868. ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: Neither, until you've checked them. Start by looking at where each writer got their information. Does either of them cite anything?

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: The district website mentions a book of land records. The blog doesn't give any sources at all.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: ___3___ A date with nothing to back it up is only a claim.

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: But the blogger says his grandfather helped to dig it. Doesn't that count for something?

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: Family memories can be valuable, ___4___ If his grandfather had worked on the canal in 1840, he'd have been well over a hundred when the blogger was born.

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: Oh, I hadn't thought of that. So should we just ignore the blog completely?

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. ___5___ It shows how local people remember the canal, even if the date itself is wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: That's a nice idea. ___6___ We found it on a social media page called 'Old Saen Rak'.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: It's a lovely picture, but does the page say who took it, or when?

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: No. The caption just says 'the good old days'.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: Then it's hard to use it as evidence of anything specific. ___7___ The city archive has hundreds of dated photographs, and most of them can be used in school projects free of charge.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Orawan
dialogue.text: Of course not. Pull up a chair and I'll show you how the online catalogue works.

dialogue.speaker: Beam
dialogue.text: Thank you so much. This is going to make our project far more convincing.

options: We've decided to leave the sources section until last,
Our teacher has already checked every source for us,
We've only managed to find a couple of short articles,
We've got more material than we know what to do with,
items.explanationTh: Ms Orawan ตอบว่า "that's a good problem to have" ซึ่งใช้กับปัญหาที่เกิดจากการมีมากเกินไป และ Beam พูดต่อว่า "which of it" แสดงว่ามีข้อมูลจำนวนมาก ตัวลวงที่มีบทความน้อยไม่ใช่ "ปัญหาที่ดี" ส่วนการที่ครูตรวจให้แล้วขัดกับการไม่แน่ใจว่าเชื่อถือได้ไหม

options: Could we simply take the average of the two dates?
Which of the two should we go with?
Why would a district office publish the wrong date?
Should we just use the blog, as it's more detailed?
items.explanationTh: คำตอบ "Neither, until you've checked them." ใช้ตอบคำถามที่ให้เลือกระหว่างสองสิ่ง จึงต้องเป็น "Which of the two..." ตัวลวงที่เป็นคำถาม yes/no หรือคำถาม Why ไม่สามารถตอบด้วย Neither ได้

options: In that case, it doesn't matter which one you use.
Then the blog is probably the more reliable of the two.
Then you should cite the blog rather than the website.
Then I'd treat the blog with a good deal of caution.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคถัดมา "A date with nothing to back it up is only a claim." แสดงว่าบล็อกที่ไม่มีแหล่งอ้างอิงควรระวัง ตัวลวงทั้งสามขัดกับเหตุผลนี้ เพราะยกให้บล็อกน่าเชื่อถือกว่า หรือบอกว่าใช้อันไหนก็ได้

options: and this one fits perfectly with the land records.
so it's safer to trust them over written records.
but the numbers here don't quite add up.
which is why I'd use the blog as your main source.
items.explanationTh: Ms Orawan คำนวณให้เห็นว่าถ้าปู่ขุดคลองปี 1840 ปู่จะอายุเกินร้อยปีตอนผู้เขียนบล็อกเกิด แปลว่าตัวเลขไม่สมเหตุสมผล จึงต้องเป็น "don't quite add up" ตัวลวงอื่นสนับสนุนบล็อก ซึ่งขัดกับการคำนวณนี้

options: You should delete it from your notes right away.
You'd better ask the blogger to correct it first.
You could still mention it as an example of local memory.
You could use its date if you add a footnote.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคต่อมา "It shows how local people remember the canal, even if the date itself is wrong" บอกคุณค่าของบล็อกในฐานะความทรงจำของคนท้องถิ่น ตัวลวงเรื่องใช้วันที่ของบล็อกพร้อมเชิงอรรถขัดกับ "the date itself is wrong" และการลบทิ้งขัดกับ "Not necessarily"

options: What about this photo of boats on the canal?
Do we really need to include any photos at all?
Is it all right to copy text from social media?
Can we use photos that we've taken ourselves?
items.explanationTh: Mai พูดต่อว่า "We found it on a social media page" และ Ms Orawan ตอบว่า "It's a lovely picture" คำถามจึงต้องพูดถึงภาพหนึ่งภาพที่พบออนไลน์ ตัวลวงเรื่องภาพที่ถ่ายเองขัดกับการพบบนโซเชียลมีเดีย และเรื่องการคัดลอกข้อความไม่ใช่ picture

options: You'd better pay the page owner to use it instead.
You might have more luck elsewhere.
I'm afraid there are no other photos of the canal.
You could use it as your cover without a credit.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคต่อมาแนะนำหอจดหมายเหตุของเมืองที่มีภาพระบุวันที่หลายร้อยภาพ จึงเป็นการบอกให้ไปหาแหล่งอื่น ตัวลวง "no other photos" ขัดกับข้อมูลนี้ และการใช้ภาพโดยไม่ให้เครดิตหรือจ่ายเงินเจ้าของเพจไม่ได้นำไปสู่การแนะนำหอจดหมายเหตุ

options: Then why did you say it was hard to use them?
Would you mind showing us how to find them?
Do you happen to know when the archive opens?
So we can't use them in our final report, then?
items.explanationTh: "Of course not. Pull up a chair and I'll show you..." เป็นคำตอบรับแบบสุภาพของคำขอ "Would you mind...?" (ไม่รังเกียจ) แล้วสาธิตวิธีค้นให้ ตัวลวงเรื่องใช้ภาพไม่ได้ขัดกับ "free of charge" ส่วนคำถามเรื่องเวลาเปิดตอบด้วย "Of course not" ไม่ได้

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่ถูกต้องที่สุด
groups.title: The Loom Desk
groups.text:
THE LOOM DESK — Co-working on Charoen Wiang Road
Quiet focus downstairs. Friendly buzz upstairs.

Whether you're a freelancer, a start-up team or a student with a thesis to finish, The Loom Desk gives you a professional place to work without the cost of renting an office.

Plans (prices per month)
• Hot Desk — 1,900 baht: any free seat on the upper floor, 8:00–20:00
• Quiet Desk — 2,600 baht: your own fixed seat in the silent zone downstairs, open 24 hours
• Team Room — 9,500 baht: a lockable room for up to four people, open 24 hours

Every plan includes high-speed Wi-Fi, unlimited coffee and tea, and six hours of meeting-room time per month. Additional meeting-room hours cost 150 baht each (student discounts do not apply to these).

Students with a valid university ID get 30% off the Hot Desk plan; the discounted plan can be used on weekdays only.

Not ready to commit? Book a free trial day online — no credit card required.
Please note: phone calls are not permitted in the silent zone. Call booths are available on both floors.

items.stem: Who would the Quiet Desk plan suit best?
options: A freelancer who takes client calls at her desk
A student looking for the cheapest weekday seat
A writer who likes to work alone late at night
A team of four that needs a room it can lock
items.explanationTh: Quiet Desk เป็นที่นั่งประจำในโซนเงียบและเปิด 24 ชั่วโมง จึงเหมาะกับนักเขียนที่ทำงานคนเดียวตอนดึก ตัวลวงเรื่องคุยโทรศัพท์ที่โต๊ะขัดกับ "phone calls are not permitted in the silent zone" ทีมสี่คนเหมาะกับ Team Room และนักศึกษาที่อยากได้ราคาถูกสุดควรใช้ Hot Desk ที่มีส่วนลด

items.stem: A university student takes the discounted Hot Desk plan and uses eight hours of meeting-room time in one month. How much does she pay?

groups.text:
SAENG ARUN FOUNDATION
Bridge Scholarships 2027 — Call for Applications

The Saeng Arun Foundation invites applications from Grade 12 students who plan to study engineering, agriculture or public health at a Thai university from June 2027.

Each scholarship covers full tuition for up to four years plus a monthly living allowance of 6,000 baht. Recipients must maintain a GPA of at least 2.75. Anyone who falls below this level for two consecutive semesters will lose the allowance, although tuition support will continue for one further semester while they receive academic coaching.

Eligibility
• Current GPA of 3.00 or above
• Household income below 30,000 baht per month
• Not already holding another full scholarship

How to apply
Submit the online form, your transcript and a 500-word essay describing a problem in your home community by 15 January 2027. Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed in February. Late or incomplete applications will not be considered.

In return, recipients are asked to mentor two younger students from their former school during their second year of study.

groups.title: Review: Hotel Tamarisk, Ban Pha Daeng
groups.text:
I booked three nights at Hotel Tamarisk largely because of its photographs: whitewashed rooms, a rooftop terrace and a view across the rice fields to the hills. The view, I am pleased to report, is every bit as lovely in person. Almost everything else was a little less polished than the pictures had led me to expect.

Let me start with the positives. The staff could hardly have been more welcoming. When my train arrived two hours late, the night manager not only waited up to check me in but had kept a bowl of noodle soup warm in the kitchen. Breakfast, served on the terrace, was another highlight, with fruit from the owners' own orchard and excellent coffee.

The rooms are another matter. Mine was clean and spacious, but the air conditioner rattled so loudly that I ended up switching it off and opening the window, only to be woken at five by a neighbouring farm's roosters. The "high-speed" Wi-Fi was anything but; after two failed attempts to join a video call, I gave up and worked from a café in town. When I mentioned these problems, the manager apologised and moved me to a quieter room, which I appreciated, although its shower took an age to run hot.

At 1,800 baht a night, the Tamarisk is not expensive for the area, and travellers who want peace, scenery and genuine hospitality will find plenty to like. Anyone who needs to work while travelling, however, should look elsewhere — or at least pack a pair of earplugs and some patience.

Rating: 3/5

groups.title: Doi Kram to ration tap water as reservoir shrinks
groups.text:
DOI KRAM — Residents of Doi Kram will receive tap water on a rotating schedule from 1 March, after the town's main reservoir fell to its lowest level in eleven years.

Under a plan announced by the municipal water authority on Tuesday, the town will be divided into three zones, each of which will receive water for sixteen hours a day. Hospitals, schools and the fire station will be exempt and will continue to have a constant supply. The authority expects the measure to cut daily consumption by about 18 percent, allowing the reservoir, now at 23 percent of its capacity, to last until the rains normally arrive in late May.

Authority director Supaporn Rakdee urged residents not to fill large containers just before their supply is switched off. "If everyone stockpiles water at the same moment, pressure will drop across the whole network and the plan will fail," she warned.

Reaction has been mixed. Owners of small guesthouses in the old town fear that tourists will cancel their bookings, and the local business association has asked for hotels to be added to the exempt list. Farmers on the edge of town, on the other hand, say the plan does not go far enough. "We were told to cut our irrigation by half last month. It's only fair that households share the burden," said rice grower Anan Kaewmanee.

The authority has also promised to repair leaking pipes, which it estimates lose nearly a quarter of all treated water before it reaches homes. Work in the central zone is due to begin next month.

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่ถูกต้องที่สุด
groups.title: Living Light
groups.text:
On certain summer nights, swimmers off some tropical coasts notice something strange: every stroke they make leaves a trail of blue sparks in the water. The light is not reflected moonlight, nor is it a sign of pollution. It is produced by countless single-celled organisms called dinoflagellates, which glow briefly whenever the water around them is disturbed. They are among thousands of species capable of bioluminescence, the production of light by a living thing.

The chemistry behind this light is surprisingly similar across very different organisms. In most cases, a molecule known as a luciferin reacts with oxygen, a process speeded up by an enzyme called a luciferase. The reaction releases its energy almost entirely as light rather than heat, which is why bioluminescence is sometimes described as "cold light". An ordinary light bulb, by comparison, wastes much of its energy warming the air around it. Yet the details vary: the luciferins of fireflies, jellyfish and deep-sea shrimp are not all the same molecule, and biologists believe that the ability to glow has evolved independently dozens of times.

That repeated invention hints at how useful light can be, especially in the ocean. Below about 200 metres, sunlight fades to almost nothing, and in this vast darkness the majority of animals are thought to produce light of some kind. They use it in strikingly different ways. The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure in front of its mouth to tempt curious prey within reach. Some squid release clouds of luminous ink to confuse attackers, much as their shallow-water relatives use dark ink. Perhaps the cleverest strategy is counter-illumination: many fish and shrimp have light organs along their bellies that match the faint glow from above, so that a predator looking up sees no shadow to give them away.

The dinoflagellates' sparks may serve a defensive purpose too, though a less obvious one. According to what is known as the "burglar alarm" hypothesis, the flash does not frighten off the tiny animals that graze on these organisms. Instead, it makes the grazers themselves visible to larger fish, which may then eat them. A grazer that sets off the alarm, in other words, risks becoming a meal.

On land, bioluminescence is far rarer, and fireflies are its best-known example. Here, light serves mainly as a language. Each species flashes in its own pattern of timing and colour, allowing the insects to recognise members of their own kind in the dark. In a few places, thousands of fireflies gathered in riverside trees flash almost in unison, a display that has drawn growing numbers of visitors and raised concerns that boat traffic and bright lights may be disrupting the very signals the insects depend on.

Scientists, meanwhile, have found practical uses for these natural lamps. Because the luciferase reaction produces light only when certain molecules are present, researchers can insert the genes responsible into other cells and use the resulting glow to follow processes that would otherwise be invisible. In laboratories, glowing markers now reveal whether a particular gene has been switched on, or whether a water sample contains harmful bacteria. Some designers have even imagined trees that could light streets at night, although such ideas remain a long way from reality.

What began as a chemical trick has, it seems, been reinvented again and again wherever darkness made light worth having.

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่ถูกต้องที่สุด
groups.title: Work by the Task
groups.text:
Ten years ago, a student in need of extra money might have looked for a weekend job in a shop or restaurant. Today, many simply open an app. With a few taps, they can deliver meals, design logos, translate documents or assemble furniture for strangers, choosing when and how much to work. This way of earning a living, in which people are paid for individual tasks rather than holding a steady job, has become known as the gig economy, a term borrowed from musicians, who are traditionally hired one performance, or "gig", at a time.

For many workers, the main attraction is flexibility. A survey of 2,000 app-based workers in the city of Pran Nakhon found that nearly two thirds valued being able to set their own hours above any other feature of the work. Parents fit deliveries around the school run; students take on design projects between exams; retirees use the apps to stay active and add to their pensions. For people who struggle to get hired through traditional routes, such as those without formal qualifications, platforms can also offer a first foothold in paid work.

Critics argue, however, that this freedom comes at a considerable cost. Because gig workers are usually classed as independent contractors rather than employees, they are generally not entitled to sick pay, paid holidays or employer contributions to a pension. Income can also be unpredictable. A delivery rider may earn well on a rainy evening when orders surge, then wait hours for a single job on a quiet afternoon. And since platforms can change their rates at any time, a worker's earnings may fall overnight without any negotiation.

Another concern is the role of algorithms. On most platforms, it is software, not a human manager, that decides who receives which task. Workers often say they do not understand why their share of jobs suddenly drops, and some feel pressured to accept every offer for fear that turning one down will lower their rating. In this sense, the flexibility that attracted them in the first place may be less real than it appears: a worker is technically free to log off, but doing so may come at a price.

Governments have begun to respond, though in different ways. Some have created a "third category" of worker, somewhere between employee and contractor, which guarantees a minimum level of protection without removing flexibility altogether. Others require platforms to explain in plain language how their algorithms hand out work. Platform companies, for their part, warn that heavy regulation could push up prices for customers and reduce the number of tasks available, ultimately harming the very workers it is meant to protect.

What seems clear is that the gig economy is unlikely to disappear. For students considering it, the sensible approach may be to treat app-based work as one option among several: useful for building skills and earning money on their own terms, but not something to depend on without understanding the trade-offs. As one rider in the Pran Nakhon survey put it, "I'm my own boss — until the app decides I'm not."

groups.title: Paths nobody planned
groups.text:
Walk through almost any city park and you will find them: narrow strips of bare earth cutting across the grass, worn smooth by thousands of feet. Planners call them "desire paths", and they usually appear wherever the official route forces people to take the long way round. They are, in effect, shortcuts that ___1___ the route the designers had in mind.

To some park managers, such paths are simply damage. They put up fences or plant thorny hedges, only to find a new path forming a few metres away. Part of the problem is that most people are not used to ___2___ where to walk, especially when the reason is not obvious. Had designers watched how people actually moved through the space, many of these paths ___3___ in the first place.

Other planners treat desire paths as free information, since they reveal precisely where people want to go. ___4___, some universities now leave the grass around a new building unpaved for its first year. The students, ___5___ footsteps gradually trace the most natural routes, effectively design the network themselves. Only after that are the worn lines turned into proper paths.

It is a small idea, but a revealing one: sometimes the best plan is to wait and see what people do.

groups.title: Reading the rings
groups.text:
Cut across the trunk of a tree from a temperate forest and you will usually see a series of rings, one for each year of growth. Counting them reveals the tree's age, but the rings hold far more information than that. In a warm, wet year a tree grows quickly and lays down a wide ring; in a dry year, growth may slow to ___1___ an extent that the ring is barely visible.

By measuring thousands of rings, scientists can ___2___ the rainfall of periods long before anyone kept weather records. A single tree, of course, covers only its own lifetime, although one pine on a remote mountainside is thought ___3___ for more than four thousand years. To go further back, researchers match the patterns in living trees with those in old timber. ___4___ enough overlapping samples are available, the record can be stretched back thousands of years without a break.

The method has practical uses, too. When a village in the north wanted to know how old its meeting hall really was, the community had several of its roof beams ___5___ by a university team. The rings showed that the trees had been cut down more than a century earlier than local stories claimed.

groups.title: Behind the lost-property counter
groups.text:
Every day, the lost-property office at Thanawat Central Station receives around two hundred forgotten items. Umbrellas and phone chargers make up most of the pile, but staff have also logged a box of live crabs, a set of drums and, on one memorable morning, a full-sized cello. Whoever left it on the 7:15 express ___1___ in a tremendous hurry, as the case was found lying open with the bow still on the seat.

Staff say that speed matters: the longer an item sits on the shelves, ___3___ likely its owner is to come back for it. After three months, items that nobody comes forward to ___4___ are donated to charity or, in the case of documents, securely destroyed.

At present, passengers have to visit the office in person or phone during working hours. With the number of items rising every year, several members of staff feel it is high time the station ___5___ an online search system, so that owners could check from home before making a journey.

groups.text:
